base_2024.note: These values follow the cited FEC PDF snapshot, including 75,017,613 Harris votes; other votes are total minus Harris minus Trump. They are independent of the county-summed presidential totals used elsewhere in the app.

transitions.precision: About nine-in-ten for both, not exact 90.0% measurements

entrants.note: All new/returning voters, including those too young for 2016. Other is residual from rounded shares.
All new/returning voters, including those too young for 2020. Other is residual from rounded shares.

notes: The 2028 nominees are unspecified. Harris and Trump label 2024 voter cohorts, not the 2028 candidates.
Historical turnout records are validated; candidate choice is self-reported. These are panel estimates, not candidate vote-total ratios.
The 2020 report notes revised 2020 survey weighting in later releases. Its about-nine-in-ten statement is used as an approximate benchmark only.
Historical cohort transitions refer to citizens with reliable panel data and should not be interpreted as tracking all original voters through death, migration or eligibility changes.
2028 defaults, entrant volume, and midterm-return assumptions are analyst illustrations, not polling or a forecast. No 2026 House margin is carried into the presidential calculation.
Historical House margins are rounded to one decimal; presidential margins here subtract published FEC vote shares. The House-to-House 2008–2010 swing is 17.4 points toward Republicans.
Pre-Trump results provide historical context; their coalitions are not assumed interchangeable with the 2024 coalitions.
